title: Streamlining Subscription Management for Boutique SaaS
business: A boutique SaaS provider managing recurring billing for niche software tools.
problem: Manual database schema management and fragmented controller logic lead to inconsistent billing states and high maintenance costs when adding new subscription tiers.
solution: Ruby on Rails utilizes the Active Record pattern to encapsulate business logic directly within models, ensuring that state transitions for subscriptions are consistent and automatically mapped to the underlying database schema.
steps: Define the Subscription model using Active Record to encapsulate billing state logic.
Configure routes to map subscription endpoints to the SubscriptionController.
Implement controller actions to process incoming subscription requests and parameters.
Use model callbacks to trigger asynchronous background jobs for billing updates.
Render subscription views using Action View to display current status to users.
outcome: A unified, maintainable codebase where business rules are centralized, reducing the risk of data corruption during subscription lifecycle changes.
limitation: The tight coupling of business logic to models can lead to 'fat models' that become difficult to test as the application grows; verify this by monitoring the cyclomatic complexity of model methods.

code.content:
class Subscription < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :user
  # Encapsulates state logic within the model
  after_save_commit :process_billing, if: :active?

  def process_billing
    BillingJob.perform_later(self)
  end
end
code.explanation: This code demonstrates how Rails encapsulates business logic within the model, using callbacks to trigger background jobs automatically when a subscription state changes.
